📰 Democrats want Trump's Grok chats saved after reports he asked it about Venezuela

Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia, the top Democrats on the House Judiciary and Oversight committees, sent Trump a letter asking him to preserve "any prompts" he gave AI chatbots such as Grok, ChatGPT and Claude for official duties, plus the answers, Politico reports.

The trigger is a Time report. In December 2025, about a month before the US captured Nicolás Maduro, Trump spent hours talking to Musk's Grok, a source told Time, including asking how Venezuelans would react to Maduro's capture. Grok said many would likely celebrate.

"You consulted Grok—but not Congress," the letter says. The two want a briefing by 5 p.m. on November 11, and could chair those committees if Democrats win the House next week.

A White House official said it "preserves all required records in accordance with the law."

📉 Google just lost $500 billion in a day, and its own AI is part of why

Alphabet stock fell about 13% on Thursday, its worst day since Google went public in 2004. Roughly $500 billion in market value vanished, the second-biggest one-day wipeout in US history after Nvidia's $589 billion drop in January 2025.

Searches grew at their fastest pace in five years. Search revenue still missed forecasts, growing 12%, down from 19% in the first quarter. A Google executive told investors part of the reason is AI Mode, Google's chatbot-style search, which shows fewer ads.

Meanwhile AI spending hit $51.4 billion in the quarter and free cash flow went to minus $9.1 billion, three times worse than analysts expected. Google says spending will "increase significantly" again in 2027.

Cloud, the part that sells AI to companies, more than doubled to nearly $31 billion, per CNBC.
